retirement:search: Searches judged adequate for this narrow, short-lived exemption: the USC and eCFR citation searches (complete, 0 hits) exclude any current-law reference, and the OFR catalog search (1937 onward, coverage warning) is supplemented by my own bounded search, on 2026-10-19, of the held WPA 1944 numbered list (jobs/x1-class-engine/data/WPA_NUMBERED_ENTRIES.csv, every numbered entry) and of all 526 held Hoover OFR 1974 compilation texts (jobs/ofr-compilations/output/texts) for each exempted person's surname. That search found the serial extension orders that do exist for other persons in this family (EO 6615 and EO 6974 for Jacob L. Nuber, EO 6975 for Charles J. James) but no later order naming the person(s) exempted by this order.
retirement:statute: Authority check: section 204 of Part II of the Legislative Appropriation Act of June 30, 1932 (Economy Act). No held source shows repeal or amendment of section 204 before this order's stated end date; the held WPA entries for EO 6615 (Feb. 26, 1934) and EO 6974/6975 (Feb. 1935) show the President still granting exemptions from the compulsory retirement provisions after this order's end, which corroborates that the statutory scheme (and so the exemption's object) continued through the stated date.
retirement:savings: Service performed and compensation earned while the exemption ran are accrued effects; the order creates no continuing duty, office or rule after its stated term, and no later order names it.
retirement:indep: The order contains a single operative command (the time-limited exemption); the recital of authority and the identification of the employee(s) are not independent commands. No retained independent command survives the stated term.
retirement:earlyend: Own-terms expiry on the stated date. An individual employee's death or voluntary separation before that date would leave the exemption unused but is not, on the order's text, a termination of the order; no held record shows any such event, and no later order amends, revokes or extends this order before the stated date (see search). The until-date is a fixed term of the grant, not a deadline or not-later-than bound on some other act.
